metadata.question: In the Norwegian Sea during Septermber 19, 2019, is the water color at (46.694935, -50.925784) more milky than (46.809436, -58.528990)?

data.raw_code: The user is asking about water color comparison between two points in the Norwegian Sea on September 19, 2019. They want to know if one location has more "milky" water than the other. For water color analysis, I should use: 1. Sentinel-2 imagery (good for water analysis with high resolution) 2. Focus on bands that can detect turbidity/milky water - typically using reflectance in visible bands 3. For "milky" water, I could use turbidity indices or simply compare reflectance in blue/green bands Good approaches: - Compare reflectance in blue band (B2) - milky water typically has higher reflectance - Use turbidity index like (B4/B2) or similar - Focus on September 19, 2019 specifically I need to: 1. Define both points as geometries 2. Get Sentinel-2 imagery for that specific date 3. Mask clouds 4. Extract reflectance values at both points 5. Compare to determine which is more "milky" For milky water detection, higher reflectance in visible bands (especially blue/green) typically indicates more suspended sediments/turbidity. Let me structure this: - Use Sentinel-2 MSI - Get images for September 19, 2019 - Extract blue band (B2) reflectance at both points - Compare values - higher reflectance = more milky - Handle cases where no data or no valid pixels ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const point1 = ee.Geometry.Point([-50.925784, 46.694935]); const point2 = ee.Geometry.Point([-58.528990, 46.809436]); const date = '2019-09-19'; // 2. Data Acquisition - Sentinel-2 for water color analysis const s2Col = ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED') .filterDate(date, ee.Date(date).advance(1, 'day')) .filterBounds(ee.Geometry.Point([-54.726387, 46.752185])) // Center between points .filter(ee.Filter.lt('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE', 80)); const colSize = s2Col.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Sentinel-2 images on ${date}: ${colSize}`); if (colSize === 0) { console.log("No Sentinel-2 images found for the date."); console.log("C1"); return; } // Get the best image (least cloudy) const image = s2Col.sort('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE').first(); // 3. Cloud masking function maskS2clouds(image) { const qa = image.select('QA60'); const cloudBitMask = 1 << 10; const cirrusBitMask = 1 << 11; const mask = qa.bitwiseAnd(cloudBitMask).eq(0) .and(qa.bitwiseAnd(cirrusBitMask).eq(0)); return image.updateMask(mask); } const maskedImage = maskS2clouds(image); // 4. Extract blue band reflectance (B2) for milky water detection const blueBand = 'B2'; // 490nm - good for detecting turbidity // Get reflectance values at both points const val1 = maskedImage.select(blueBand).reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: point1, scale: 100, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get(blueBand); const val2 = maskedImage.select(blueBand).reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: point2, scale: 100, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get(blueBand); const reflectance1 = val1.getInfo(); const reflectance2 = val2.getInfo(); console.log(`Point 1 blue reflectance: ${reflectance1}`); console.log(`Point 2 blue reflectance: ${reflectance2}`); // 5. Validation & Final Answer if (reflectance1 === null || reflectance2 === null) { console.log("One or both points have no valid data"); console.log("C2"); } else if (isNaN(reflectance1) || isNaN(reflectance2)) { console.log("Invalid reflectance values"); console.log("C3"); } else { // Higher blue reflectance = more milky water (more suspended particles) if (reflectance1 > reflectance2) { console.log("Point 1 has higher reflectance - more milky"); console.log("A"); } else { console.log("Point 2 has higher reflectance - more milky"); console.log("B"); } } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
